passage:
For three evenings Mahima watched her cousin Sharmila leave the groundnut shelling half done and hurry toward the bank kiosk by the bus stop, phone pressed to her ear. At night Sharmila slept with the phone under her pillow and jumped whenever it buzzed.
On the fourth evening Mahima waited on the step until Sharmila came back, dusty and out of breath.
'Sit for a minute,' Mahima said, pushing the bowl toward her. 'You don't have to tell me anything. I've just noticed you running to the kiosk every day.'
Sharmila shelled two pods in silence. 'It's a prize. They need a tax first.'
Mahima didn't scold. 'Then it can wait one night. Tomorrow we'll call the bank's own number from your passbook, together. If it's real, it will still be real.'
Sharmila let out a long breath and nodded.

qa.q: Where did Sharmila hurry to each evening?
qa.a: Sharmila hurried toward the bank kiosk by the bus stop.

qa.q: What does Sharmila's long breath at the end suggest?
qa.a: It suggests relief, as if part of her had been waiting for someone to give her permission to pause.

qa.q: Which part of Mahima's approach made it easier for Sharmila to open up?
qa.a: Mahima asked without scolding, said Sharmila didn't have to explain, and suggested one night's pause and a call to the bank's own number, which felt safe rather than shaming.

qa.q: What might Sharmila have been feeling before Mahima spoke to her?
qa.a: Sharmila was probably tense and cornered, sleeping with the phone under her pillow and rushing to pay with no one to check it with.

grounding: It shows a family member noticing secrecy and hurried payments, asking gently without blame and proposing a pause to check through the bank's official number.

passage:
Sofia noticed it first on Sunday: Oskar eating toast standing up, eyes on his phone, not even hearing the kettle click off. By Wednesday he had cancelled football twice and made two bank transfers at the kitchen table, tilting the screen away from her.
On Thursday night she found him on the balcony in the cold, typing fast.
She handed him a mug of tea and leaned on the railing beside him. 'You've seemed really far away this week. I'm not angry. I just miss you.'
Oskar rubbed his face. 'There's this refund from the tax office. They say I have to pay a processing fee first. Today.'
'Okay,' Sofia said slowly. 'How about we pause till morning and ring the tax office on the number from their own website? I'll sit with you.'
He looked at the phone, then at her. 'Yeah. Okay.'

qa.q: What had Oskar cancelled twice by Wednesday?
What was Sofia feeling when she joined Oskar on the balcony?
qa.a: She was worried and missed him, but chose warmth over anger, telling him she wasn't angry and just missed him.

qa.q: What made Sofia's suggestion a good turning point?
qa.a: She proposed a short pause and a check on the number from the tax office's own website, and offered to sit with him, so he could verify without losing face.

qa.q: What might Oskar be feeling when Sofia offers to sit with him?
qa.a: He is probably relieved to share the weight, even if he is also embarrassed that his week of secrecy has been noticed.

grounding: It shows someone close noticing a person glued to the phone and making hidden transfers, then asking calmly and suggesting a pause to verify officially.
